title: OS command execution via x.execute (groovy) — review required
description: The groovy sink x.execute hands its argument to a command shell or process launcher. If any part of the argument derives from untrusted input, an attacker can inject extra commands. This lexical rule flags the sink; the reviewer confirms every argument is trusted or safely separated from the command.
remediation: Avoid the sink: use argument-vector APIs (list .execute() with separate arguments) so untrusted data never passes through a shell. If a shell is unavoidable, pin an allowlist of commands and quote every interpolated value.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: any x.execute call matches, including fully trusted invocations. Dataflow from untrusted input is not proven — treat every hit as review-required.
